requirements.quote:
As an encrypted and authenticated transport, QUIC provides a range of
   protections against denial of service.  Once the cryptographic
   handshake is complete, QUIC endpoints discard most packets that are
   not authenticated, greatly limiting the ability of an attacker to
   interfere with existing connections.
requirements.condition: The cryptographic handshake is complete and a packet is not authenticated.
requirements.required_behavior: QUIC endpoints discard most such packets.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet processing after handshake completion can be observed, but the qualification "most" does not define which unauthenticated packets may be retained.

requirements.quote:
Once a connection is established, QUIC endpoints might accept some
   unauthenticated ICMP packets (see Section 14.2.1), but the use of
   these packets is extremely limited.  The only other type of packet
   that an endpoint might accept is a stateless reset (Section 10.3),
   which relies on the token being kept secret until it is used.
requirements.condition: A connection is established and an unauthenticated packet is received.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint does not accept unauthenticated packet types other than the limited ICMP packets and Stateless Reset packets described here.
requirements.why_checkable: Accepted unauthenticated packet types can be tested, though the ICMP allowance is not fully specified within this chunk.

requirements.quote:
Once a connection is established, QUIC endpoints might accept some
   unauthenticated ICMP packets (see Section 14.2.1), but the use of
   these packets is extremely limited.  The only other type of packet
   that an endpoint might accept is a stateless reset (Section 10.3),
   which relies on the token being kept secret until it is used.
requirements.condition: A Stateless Reset token has not yet been used.
requirements.required_behavior: The Stateless Reset token is kept secret until it is used.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The token is not disclosed before use.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation can be inspected or instrumented to determine whether a reset token is exposed before its use.

requirements.quote:
During the creation of a connection, QUIC only provides protection
   against attacks from off the network path.  All QUIC packets contain
   proof that the recipient saw a preceding packet from its peer.
requirements.condition: Any QUIC packet is constructed or validated.
requirements.required_behavior: The packet contains proof that its recipient saw a preceding packet from its peer.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A QUIC packet lacks such proof.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet construction and validation can be checked for the protocol element that supplies proof of receipt of a preceding peer packet.

requirements.quote:
Addresses cannot change during the handshake, so endpoints can
   discard packets that are received on a different network path.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: An address changes during the handshake.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation's connection state can be observed across the handshake to verify that address changes are not accepted.

requirements.quote:
Addresses cannot change during the handshake, so endpoints can
   discard packets that are received on a different network path.
requirements.condition: During the handshake, a packet is received on a network path different from the established path.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to discard the packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A focused test can deliver a handshake packet on a different path and observe whether the implementation supports the permitted discard behavior, but discarding is optional.

requirements.quote:
The Source and Destination Connection ID fields are the primary means
   of protection against an off-path attack during the handshake; see
   Section 8.1.  These are required to match those set by a peer.
requirements.condition: Source and Destination Connection ID fields are processed during the handshake.
requirements.required_behavior: The Source and Destination Connection ID fields match the values set by the peer.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A Source or Destination Connection ID field differs from the corresponding value set by the peer.
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake packets can be generated with matching and mismatching connection IDs and the endpoint's validation behavior observed.

requirements.quote:
Except for Initial and Stateless Resets, an endpoint only accepts
   packets that include a Destination Connection ID field that matches a
   value the endpoint previously chose.  This is the only protection
   offered for Version Negotiation packets.
requirements.condition: The received packet is neither an Initial packet nor a Stateless Reset.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint accepts the packet only if it includes a Destination Connection ID field matching a value previously chosen by the endpoint.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint accepts such a packet when the Destination Connection ID field is absent or does not match a value previously chosen by the endpoint.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet acceptance can be tested across absent, matching, and nonmatching Destination Connection ID values for each applicable packet type.

requirements.quote:
The Destination Connection ID field in an Initial packet is selected
   by a client to be unpredictable, which serves an additional purpose.
requirements.condition: A client selects the Destination Connection ID for an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The client selects an unpredictable Destination Connection ID.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client uses a predictably selected Destination Connection ID.
requirements.why_checkable: The client's connection-ID generation algorithm and generated samples can be evaluated for unpredictability.

requirements.quote:
The packets that carry the cryptographic handshake are protected with
   a key that is derived from this connection ID and a salt specific to
   the QUIC version.  This allows endpoints to use the same process for
   authenticating packets that they receive as they use after the
   cryptographic handshake completes.  Packets that cannot be
   authenticated are discarded.  Protecting packets in this fashion
   provides a strong assurance that the sender of the packet saw the
   Initial packet and understood it.
requirements.condition: A packet carries the cryptographic handshake.
requirements.required_behavior: The packet is protected with a key derived from the Initial packet's Destination Connection ID and a salt specific to the QUIC version.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The packet is protected using a key not derived from that connection ID and the version-specific salt.
requirements.why_checkable: Known connection IDs, versions, salts, and handshake packets permit verification of the key derivation and packet protection result.

requirements.quote:
The packets that carry the cryptographic handshake are protected with
   a key that is derived from this connection ID and a salt specific to
   the QUIC version.  This allows endpoints to use the same process for
   authenticating packets that they receive as they use after the
   cryptographic handshake completes.  Packets that cannot be
   authenticated are discarded.  Protecting packets in this fashion
   provides a strong assurance that the sender of the packet saw the
   Initial packet and understood it.
requirements.condition: An endpoint receives a packet that cannot be authenticated.
requirements.why_checkable: A packet with invalid authentication can be injected and the implementation can be checked to ensure it is discarded.

requirements.quote:
These protections are not intended to be effective against an
   attacker that is able to receive QUIC packets prior to the connection
   being established.  Such an attacker can potentially send packets
   that will be accepted by QUIC endpoints.  This version of QUIC
   attempts to detect this sort of attack, but it expects that endpoints
   will fail to establish a connection rather than recovering.  For the
   most part, the cryptographic handshake protocol [QUIC-TLS] is
   responsible for detecting tampering during the handshake.
requirements.condition: An on-path attacker tampers with packets before the connection is established and the attack is detected.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint fails to establish the connection rather than recovering from the attack.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint recovers and establishes the connection after the detected attack.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can tamper with handshake traffic and observe whether connection establishment fails instead of recovering.

requirements.quote:
These protections are not intended to be effective against an
   attacker that is able to receive QUIC packets prior to the connection
   being established.  Such an attacker can potentially send packets
   that will be accepted by QUIC endpoints.  This version of QUIC
   attempts to detect this sort of attack, but it expects that endpoints
   will fail to establish a connection rather than recovering.  For the
   most part, the cryptographic handshake protocol [QUIC-TLS] is
   responsible for detecting tampering during the handshake.
requirements.condition: Packets are tampered with during the handshake.
requirements.required_behavior: The cryptographic handshake protocol detects the tampering.
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake traffic can be altered and the handshake implementation observed for detection, but "for the most part" leaves the exact responsibility and coverage unclear.

requirements.quote:
Endpoints are permitted to use other methods to detect and attempt to
   recover from interference with the handshake.  Invalid packets can be
   identified and discarded using other methods, but no specific method
   is mandated in this document.
requirements.condition: An endpoint encounters interference with the handshake.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to use additional methods to detect and attempt recovery from the interference.
requirements.why_checkable: Implementation inspection can identify additional detection or recovery methods, but the text explicitly mandates no particular method or outcome.

requirements.quote:
Endpoints are permitted to use other methods to detect and attempt to
   recover from interference with the handshake.  Invalid packets can be
   identified and discarded using other methods, but no specific method
   is mandated in this document.
requirements.condition: An invalid packet is identified using an additional implementation-specific method.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to discard the invalid packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Invalid packets recognized by an implementation-specific method can be supplied and their disposition observed, but discarding and the identification method are optional.
